extracted.intended_audience: parties, counsel, and staff participating in FCC adjudicatory/hearing proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory procedural rules (47 CFR Part 1) governing designation of presiding officers, prehearing practices, motions, discovery, hearings, decisions, appeals, and related adjudicatory matters before the Federal Communications Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to modify/enlarge issues — timeliness and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to modify the issues must be filed within prescribed periods; late motions require a showing of why it was not possible to file on time and will be granted only if good cause is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For program carriage complaints referred to a presiding officer, motions shall be filed within 15 calendar days after the deadline for submitting written appearances, except persons not named as parties may file such motions with petitions to intervene up to 30 days after publication of the designation order in the Federal Register. Motions based on new or newly discovered facts must be filed within 15 days after discovery. In absence of good cause, late motions will be considered on the merits only if they raise a question of probable decisional significance and such substantial public interest importance as to warrant consideration despite untimely filing. Such motions, oppositions, and replies must contain specific allegations of fact supported by affidavits of persons with personal knowledge; facts of which official notice may be taken are excepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of potential forfeiture for misconduct allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: When issues are enlarged to inquire into alleged applicant misconduct during the application process, the enlargement must include notice of potential forfeiture liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The enlarged issues must include notice that after hearings and upon a finding that alleged misconduct occurred and warrants penalty, the applicant may be liable for a forfeiture of up to the maximum statutory amount (see 47 U.S.C. 503(b)(2)(A)), in addition to or in lieu of denying the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of presiding officer — who may preside
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing proceedings will be conducted by a presiding officer identified in the order designating a matter for hearing; only the Commission, one or more commissioners, or an administrative law judge designated pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 3105 may be designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise stated, 'presiding officer' includes the Commission when it designates itself. If a presiding officer becomes unavailable during a hearing, another presiding officer will be designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of case manager when Commission is presiding
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission designates itself as presiding officer, it may delegate authority to a case manager to develop the record in a written hearing; the case manager must be a staff attorney who qualifies as a neutral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission shall not designate staff who participated in identifying issues for hearing, who have taken or will take an active part in investigating, prosecuting, or advocating in the case, or who are expected to investigate and act upon petitions to deny, to serve as case manager or to advise/assist the case manager. A case manager may perform any functions generally performed by a presiding officer except: resolving new or novel issues, issuing orders on the merits resolving issues designated for hearing, issuing orders on motions for summary decision under § 1.251, or performing other functions the Commission reserves to itself in the order appointing the case manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority/powers of the presiding officer
rubrics_metrics.description: From designation until decision or transfer, the presiding officer has specified authority granted by law and the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated authority includes: administer oaths and affirmations; issue subpoenas; examine witnesses; rule upon questions of evidence; take or cause depositions; regulate the course of the hearing, maintain decorum, and exclude disruptive persons; require memoranda of law and oral argument on legal questions; hold conferences for settlement/simplification of issues; dispose of procedural requests and ancillary matters; take actions and make decisions in conformity with governing law; act on motions to enlarge/modify/delete hearing issues; act on in forma pauperis motions under § 1.224; decide a matter upon the existing record or request additional information; and issue orders and conduct proceedings to best conduce to the proper dispatch of business and the ends of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and qualifications of settlement officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may request appointment of a settlement officer to facilitate resolution; appointment procedures, neutrality, and limitations are prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests may be filed no later than 15 days prior to commencement of hearings (or 15 days before the affirmative case filing deadline in written-record hearings). The presiding officer may appoint a neutral (as defined in 5 U.S.C. 571 and 573) if it appears appointment will facilitate settlement. Parties may request a settlement officer of their choosing if the person is a neutral; appointment is subject to approval of all parties. The Commission, any sitting Commissioners, and the presiding officer cannot serve as settlement officer. Staff who qualify as neutrals may serve unless their duties include drafting/recommending actions on merits of issues designated for hearing. The settlement officer may require submission of written direct cases for review, meet with parties (individual or joint), express opinions and recommend settlement means; all such meetings are off-the-record, confidential under 5 U.S.C. 574, and statements/offers are inadmissible as evidence in Commission proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification of presiding officer — procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer may withdraw if disqualified; parties may request withdrawal on grounds of personal bias or other disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The person seeking disqualification must file an affidavit detailing facts constituting grounds. The presiding officer may respond and rule. The seeker may appeal a denial within five days of the presiding officer's ruling; failure to appeal waives the right. If appealed, the presiding officer certifies the question, affidavit, and any response to the Commission and the hearing is suspended pending the Commission's ruling, which may be made with or without hearing. The affidavit, response, testimony/argument, and Commission decision become part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of facts and genuineness of documents — timing and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may serve written requests for admission of genuineness of documents or truth of any relevant matters of fact within specified timeframes; matters are deemed admitted unless timely responded to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must include clear copies of documents. Requests may be served within 20 days after the time for filing a notice of appearance has expired, within 20 days after an order adding parties or changing issues, or within such shorter/longer time as the presiding officer allows. Each requested matter is deemed admitted unless the responding party serves, within the period designated (not less than 10 days after service unless presiding officer allows otherwise), either: (1) a sworn statement denying specifically the matters or setting forth reasons why the party cannot truthfully admit or deny, where a denial must fairly meet the substance and specify any partial admissions/qualifications; or (2) written objections asserting privilege, irrelevance, or impropriety. If part of a request is objected to, remainder must be answered. A copy of request and answer must be served on all parties and the presiding officer. Written objections may be ruled on by the presiding officer without additional pleadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status conferences — purpose, scheduling, and matters considered
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may direct or parties may request status conferences to consider matters relevant to conduct of the hearing and to adopt a schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer shall schedule an initial status conference promptly after written appearances are submitted and adopt a schedule to govern the proceeding. The scheduling order must include deadlines (e.g., motion to request oral hearing or to conduct hearing on a written record). Status conferences may consider clarifying/narrowing issues, scheduling, admissions and stipulations, discovery, motions, hearing procedure, settlement, and other matters aiding resolution. They may be conducted in person or by telephone/technology at the presiding officer's discretion. An official transcript shall be made unless waived by the presiding officer and parties; if waived, any rulings shall be memorialized in writing. Failure to appear after reasonable notice may be deemed waiver of rights to participate and will not preclude the presiding officer from conferring with those present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer statement of status conference actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer must enter into the record a statement reciting all actions taken at a status conference and incorporate stipulations and approved agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must also include any special rules deemed necessary to govern the course of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery and preservation of evidence — cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions relating to prehearing discovery and preservation of admissible evidence in hearing proceedings are governed by separate sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §§ 1.311 through 1.325 for detailed discovery and preservation rules applicable to hearing proceedings under this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary decision — timing, standard, and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may move for summary decision on all or part of the issues; motions must be timely and establish no genuine issue of material fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions must be filed at least 20 days prior to commencement of hearing or 20 days before the presiding officer's deadline for filing the affirmative case in written-record hearings, unless permission/invitation is given after deadlines. The moving party may not rest on allegations or denials but must show by affidavit or other materials that there is no genuine issue of material fact. Within 14 days after the motion, other parties may file opposition or countermotion; opposition must show a genuine issue of material fact, inability to present essential facts by affidavit for good cause, or that summary decision is inappropriate. Affidavits must be made on personal knowledge, contain facts admissible in evidence, and show the affiant's competence. The presiding officer may set matters for argument, require proposed findings/conclusions/briefs, and grant summary decision if pleadings, affidavits, discovery materials, admissions, or official notice show no genuine issue of material fact and entitlement to judgment. If opposing affidavits show inability to present facts, the presiding officer may deny, order continuance to permit affidavits/discovery, or otherwise act as just. If all issues are determined on summary decision, the hearing is terminated; partial decisions result in interlocutory memorandum opinion and continued hearing on remaining issues. Presiding officer may act to prevent abuse (e.g., rule matter inappropriate for summary decision, find bad faith or frivolous filings and refer for disciplinary or other action under § 1.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and place of hearing — specification and default location
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall specify the time and place of oral hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All oral hearings will take place at Commission Headquarters unless the presiding officer designates another location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of the hearing proceeding and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings on applications are full proceedings permitting participation by applicant and other parties, with burdens placed on the applicant unless otherwise ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the burden of proceeding with introduction of evidence upon any issue designated by the Commission and the burden of proof on all such issues are upon the applicant except as otherwise provided in the order of designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of procedure — who opens and closes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules specify which party opens and closes depending on the type of hearing (formal complaint, petition, application, protest, orders to show cause, Title II hearings, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At hearings on a formal complaint, petition, or application, the complainant/petitioner/applicant shall, unless the Commission orders otherwise, open and close. At protests, the protestant opens and closes if issues not specifically adopted by Commission; otherwise the grantee does so. At hearings on orders to show cause, cease and desist, revoke/modify station license, or similar Commission-initiated proceedings, the Commission shall open and close. At all hearings under Title II other than formal complaints/petitions/applications, the respondent shall open and close unless otherwise specified. In other cases, the Commission or presiding officer shall designate the order of presentation; intervenors follow the party in whose behalf intervention is made or the stage designated by the Commission/presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to transcript — timing and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may file motions requesting corrections to transcripts within specified timeframes and with proof of service; presiding officer rules on corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At any time during the proceeding, or as directed, but not later than 10 days after transmission to parties of the transcript of any oral conference or hearing, any party may file a motion requesting corrections, accompanied by proof of service on all other parties. Within 5 days after such motion, other parties may file pleadings in support or opposition. The presiding officer shall, by order, specify corrections to be made and serve a copy on all parties and make it part of the record. The presiding officer may sua sponte specify corrections on 5 days' notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed findings, conclusions, briefs — filing and waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may direct parties to file proposed findings of fact and conclusions, briefs, or memoranda; if not ordered, parties may seek leave to file; failure to file without good cause may be deemed waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such filings shall be filed within time prescribed by the presiding officer and must be accompanied by proof of service upon all other counsel and any unrepresented parties. In absence of a showing of good cause, failure to file when directed may be deemed a waiver of the right to participate further in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of proposed findings of fact and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed findings of fact must be detailed, particularized, and supported by citation; proposed conclusions must be separately stated; third-party limitations apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings must be set forth in serially numbered paragraphs and set out in detail and with particularity all basic evidentiary facts developed on the record, with appropriate citations to the transcript of record or exhibit relied on for each evidentiary fact. Proposed conclusions shall be separately stated. Proposed findings and conclusions submitted by a person other than an applicant may be limited to those issues which affect that person's interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing the record and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: After conclusion of hearing and submission of required materials, the presiding officer shall promptly close and certify the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record is closed after parties have submitted their evidence, filed any proposed findings and conclusions under § 1.263, and submitted any other information required by the presiding officer. After closing, the presiding officer shall certify the record and file it in the Office of the Secretary and serve notice of such certification on all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial and recommended decisions — contents and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proceeding is terminated on motion, or when the presiding officer is the Commission (with certain exceptions), the presiding officer shall prepare an initial or recommended decision and transmit it to the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each initial and recommended decision shall contain findings of fact and conclusions and the reasons/basis therefor upon all material issues of fact, law, or discretion presented on the record. Each initial decision shall also contain the appropriate rule or order and the sanction, relief or denial thereof; each recommended decision shall contain recommendations as to disposition by the Commission. Each initial decision will show the date upon which it will become effective absent exceptions, appeal, or review. When the Commission is not the presiding officer, the presiding officer's authority ceases upon filing an initial/recommended decision (or certification when no decision to be filed), but the presiding officer retains limited jurisdiction to effect certification, correct transcripts, and rule initially on awards of fees/expenses under the Equal Access to Justice Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and waiver of review functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may delegate its review function to a commissioner or panel; parties may agree to waive an initial or recommended decision and request final Commission action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegated commissioners or panels exercise the authority the Commission would have under §§ 1.273-1.282. When the Commission is the presiding officer it will not issue an initial/recommended decision. When the Commission is not the presiding officer, all parties may agree to waive an initial or recommended decision at any time before the record is closed and request the Commission to issue a final decision or order; the Commission or review authority may grant the request in whole or in part if it best conduces to proper dispatch of business and ends of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of the record to the Commission when presiding officer unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the presiding officer becomes unavailable in certain stages, the record may be certified to the Commission for decision or another presiding officer designated to continue or certify the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commission finds due and timely execution of its functions imperatively requires, it may direct that the record be certified to it for decision. If a presiding officer becomes unavailable after taking evidence has been concluded, the record shall be certified to the Commission and the Commission shall designate a new presiding officer for limited purpose of certifying the record. If unavailable after evidence-taking has commenced but before conclusion, the Commission shall designate another presiding officer to continue the proceeding; oral testimony already introduced shall not be reheard unless observation of witness demeanor is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and review of initial decision — exceptions, timing, and Commission actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may appeal initial decisions by filing exceptions within prescribed time and following format; the Commission may on its own initiative order further review and take various actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 30 days after public release of the full text of an initial decision (or other time specified), any party may appeal by filing exceptions; extensions are not routinely granted. Exceptions are consolidated with the supporting brief and must contain a table of contents, table of citations, a concise statement of the case, a statement of questions of law presented, and the argument presenting facts and law relied upon with specific reference to the record and legal materials. The Commission may, on its own initiative not later than 20 days after filing time expires, provide that an initial decision shall not become final and shall be further reviewed. The Commission may hear oral argument on exceptions, require briefs, reopen the record and/or remand for further testimony or findings, or issue a supplemental initial decision. No initial decision shall become effective before 50 days after public release unless otherwise ordered; timely filing of exceptions or Commission-initiated review stays effectiveness. If no exceptions are filed and Commission does not order review, the initial decision becomes effective and public notice given. Failure to file exceptions to a decision proposing to deny an application will be deemed lack of interest and the application may be dismissed with prejudice for failure to prosecute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and oral argument — contents, page limits, and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions must point out alleged material errors with particularity and reference the record; consolidated briefs are subject to page limits and reply/argument procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The consolidated exceptions and supporting brief must point out with particularity alleged material errors and contain specific references to transcript pages, exhibits, or orders supporting the exception; any objection not saved by exception is waived. Within the filing period for exceptions, any party may file a brief in support of an initial decision. Except by special permission, consolidated briefs and exceptions shall not exceed 25 double-spaced typewritten pages (TOC and table of citations not counted; all other contents/attachments counted). Within 10 days (or other time specified) after the exceptions filing period expires, any other party may file a reply brief not exceeding 25 double-spaced pages with TOC and table of citations. If exceptions are filed, any party may request oral argument not later than five days after time for filing replies has expired. The Commission will grant oral argument only where such presentations will assist in resolution. Within five days after release of an order designating an initial decision for oral argument, any party wishing to participate must file written notice of intention to appear; failure to file constitutes waiver. Orders scheduling oral argument will contain time allotments for each party.
